Source: Understanding Nutrition 12e by Whitney/Rolfes, Figure 6-4, page 175.
Table 17.4 Most Common Causes 
of Endocrine Dysfunction
Effect of Hyposecretion
Effect of Hypersecretion
• Too little hormone secreted by the
endocrine gland (hyposecretion)1
• Increased removal of the 
hormone from the blood
• Abnormal tissue responsiveness 
to the hormone
• Lack of target cell receptors
• Lack of an enzyme essential to 
the target cell response
• Too much hormone secreted 
by the endocrine gland 
(hypersecretion)
• Reduced plasma-protein binding
of the hormone (too much free,
biologically active hormone)
• Decreased removal of the 
hormone from the blood
• Decreased inactivation
• Decreased excretion
